Because of her vocal opposition to the war, Kryze found enemies in both the Republic and the Confederacy of Independent Systems.<ref name="DoM" /> From the start of the war, Satine characterized both governments as being overrun by extremists.<ref name="Brotherhood" /> In return, many in the Republic and Confederacy denounced Kryze as ignorant,<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /> with some opining that her positions were not true political middle ground<ref name="Brotherhood" /> and hypocritical since they believed the stubborn duchess was unwilling to collaborate with those she personally disagreed with.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /> As the Clone Wars continued, Kryze came to believe that the Republic was beyond saving,<ref name="Corruption" /> and during her struggle to maintain Mandalore's neutrality, likened it to an oppressive force. When faced with the underhanded tactics of the Republic's bureaucracy, Kryze privately concluded in her frustration that the government's constituents needed to speak up as the Senate infringed upon their rights.<ref name="DoM" /> On the nature of the Senate itself, Satine decried the body as incapable of creating good counsel and believed that it could not accomplish anything other than discord.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" />

[[File:BecLawiseLetsContinue-AFIN.png|thumb|left|250px|Despite her disdain for both governments, Kryze was willing to aid in efforts to peacefully resolve the war between the Republic and Confederacy.]]
Among members of Republic leadership, Kryze had a particular distaste for the policies and motives of Supreme Chancellor Palpatine and Vice Chair Amedda and harbored a deep mistrust of Republic authorities to help her without bias.<ref name="DoM" /> Satine, who disavowed currency and corporate interests, routinely criticized the Republic for allowing the presence of corporations and trade guilds among its ranks. Although she felt that the Senate was contaminated with greed and filled with self-serving representatives, Duchess Satine found friends and allies in Padmé Amidala<ref name="Corruption" /> and members of the Council of Neutral Systems, such as Kin Robb and Onaconda Farr.<ref name="Saw Gerrera" /> Though Kryze was friendly with and trusting of Amidala,<ref name="Corruption" /> the two were politically unallied due to Mandalore's neutrality.<ref name="SWE" /> Kryze supported the efforts of Amidala's faction to combat the Republic's military expansion<ref name="PoP" /> and later willingly moderated the failed Confederate-Republic peace conference, which Amidala was a delegate to, in her throne room<ref name="AFIN" /> despite her misgivings for both governments.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" />

In addition to her opposition to the Republic's militarist activities, Kryze also denounced the militant actions taken by the Jedi Order. During her time under the protection of Master Qui-Gon Jinn and then-Padawan Obi-Wan, Satine witnessed firsthand the peacekeeping nature the Jedi ascribed to themselves and knew them to be devoted to their cause. By the time of the Clone Wars, however, Kryze viewed the Jedi differently. Satine saw the Jedi's political affiliation with the Republic and their involvement in the war as a betrayal of their core values.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /> In her opinion, the Jedi had sacrificed their ideals for political convenience.<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /> Kryze described their reliance on violence to solve conflicts as foolhardy and compared their actions to a pseudo-crusade,<ref name="DoM" /> though she admitted that they came from a place of devotion and commitment to the Order, albeit misguided. Satine found it amusing and ironic how the Jedi adopted the attitudes and titles of military officers while promoting themselves as peacekeepers.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" />

===Relationships===
====Clan Kryze====
{{Dialogue|Satine|Bo. It's been a long time.|Korkie|It's okay, Auntie. She's on our side now.|Satine|Why are you helping now?|Bo-Katan|The enemy of my enemy is my friend.|Satine|There was a time when we weren't enemies. Perhaps that time has come again.|attr=Satine, Korkie, and Bo-Katan|src=<ref name="The Lawless" />}}
[[File:Satine_and_Korkie.png|thumb|right|250px|Satine cared deeply for her nephew Korkie.]]
Satine was close with her nephew Korkie and was very protective of him and his safety. Korkie sought to help Satine with her struggles during the Clone Wars and protect the New Mandalorians in kind. When Korkie and his friends uncovered Almec's treason, they attempted to appeal to Satine and get her help, but the duchess was concerned that they were becoming too involved and that their safety was at risk. Satine's desire to keep her nephew safe came across as belittlement to Korkie, which only made him more willing to rebel against her wishes and continue investigating. Even when tortured by Almec in prison, Satine tried to keep Korkie from suffering like her and protested the traitorous Prime Minister's attempt to put a shock collar on him.<ref name="TA" /> Korkie remained loyal to his aunt and her ideals as the Clone Wars continued, even as Maul and Pre Vizsla's takeover of Sundari took place. When Satine was deposed and imprisoned, Korkie led a rescue attempt to free his aunt, who was overjoyed to see him alive and well.<ref name="The Lawless" />

Korkie's attempt to rescue the deposed Satine reunited the former duchess with her estranged sister, Bo-Katan, whom she affectionately called "Bo."<ref name="The Lawless" /> Although Satine and Bo-Katan were close when they were younger<ref name="SWE Bo-Katan" /> and sincerely loved each other, their fierce ambitions<ref name="WOTG" /> and differing opinions about Mandalore's future estranged them<ref name="SWE Bo-Katan" /> and made them polar opposites in nearly every way. Where Bo-Katan couldn't understand Satine's idealism, Satine couldn't understand her sister's devotion to the perceived honor of the old ways<ref name="SWI 208" /> which had destroyed their world.<ref name="Collapse" /> Both Kryzes wanted what was best for their world but disagreed completely on what that meant.<ref name="Join the Battle" />

Though they were driven apart, each sister continued to care about the other in their own ways.<ref name="WOTG" /> Satine was alarmed to see her sister during her rescue, who in the intervening years had become a leading member of Death Watch. Korkie and Bo-Katan reassured the duchess that they were working together.<ref name="The Lawless" /> Though their reunion stemmed from having a common enemy in Maul,<ref name="SWI 208" /> Satine believed that she and her sister could reconcile their differences and become friends again, though her death soon after the failed rescue mission dashed that future.<ref name="The Lawless" /> Bo-Katan, despite her estrangement from and opposition to Satine, was devastated by her sister's death,<ref name="Bo-Katan Databank">{{Databank|bo-katan-kryze|Bo-Katan Kryze}}</ref> and over time came to respect her late sister for her ambition despite still not understanding her idealism.<ref name="Heroes of Mandalore" /><ref name="SWI 208" />

====Obi-Wan Kenobi====
{{Quote|I've loved you from the moment you came to my aid all those years ago.''<nowiki>" [</nowiki>'''…'''<nowiki>]</nowiki><br />"''Had you said the word, I would have left the Jedi Order.|Satine Kryze and Obi-Wan Kenobi|audio=ObiWanInLove-VoT.flac|<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" />}}
Satine Kryze first met Obi-Wan Kenobi during the Mandalorian Civil War, when he and Master Qui-Gon Jinn were sent to protect her from her enemies. The trio spent nearly a year on the run, living without knowing what the next day would bring, and the young duchess and Padawan began to develop feelings for each other.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /> Satine's idealism and hope for the future of her planet inspired and intoxicated the youthful enthusiasm of Obi-Wan.<ref name="Brotherhood" /> Though they came to love each other, neither acted on their feelings, and by the time the war ended,<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /> they parted without knowing what their lives could have been had they stayed together.<ref name="Brotherhood" /> Both Kryze and Kenobi looked back on their whirlwind relationship with regret, but they also felt relief at who they eventually grew into.<ref name="Join the Battle" /> In her later years, Satine did not hide her feelings for Obi-Wan and recognized that, despite their complicated past, he was an important part of her life, and she would never be able to forget him if she tried.<ref name="WOTG" />

[[File:ObiWanKenobi-XWingPOM.png|thumb|left|250px|Satine and Obi-Wan's many shared hardships strengthened their bond.]]
The two were reunited amid the Death Watch insurgency during the Clone Wars and managed to find their old rapport despite the long time they hadn't seen each other. At first, Kryze was cold to Obi-Wan, believing that he was acting in the interests of the Senate, but once corrected, she softened significantly and opened herself up to him.<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /> Still sharing similar personalities and a caustic sense of humor,<ref name="Saw Gerrera" /> they teased each other relentlessly, often with romantic undertones. Their camaraderie was strained again when Satine learned that Obi-Wan favored a Republic occupation of Mandalore, and they devolved into petty bickering and arguing over their differing politics. His resoluteness saddened her as he seemingly cared little for her planet's sovereignty, which she had long fought for.<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" />

Satine and Obi-Wan's anger towards each other peaked aboard the ''Coronet'', where their arguments turned into a physical standoff. Once they came under attack from the probe droids, however, they put aside their differences and fought side-by-side again. As the situation escalated and Kryze was taken captive by Prince Merrik, the duchess broke from her stalwart facade and confessed to Kenobi that she had loved him since the civil war and still did, and he admitted to her that he would have left the Jedi Order for her had she simply asked. Despite opening up to each other about how they felt for the first time, they didn't get a chance to speak about it further as Satine had to focus on her diplomacy.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /> In her struggle to preserve the peace and neutrality she had brought to Mandalore, Kryze inadvertently pushed Obi-Wan away, but he remained at her side even through her anger and difficulty with Republic officials.<ref name="DoM" />

Though the two made up after Satine won continuing neutrality, they continued on with their chosen paths as friends.<ref name="DoM" /> Both had given their existences to something bigger than themselves, and they knew any relationship was impossible despite their unshakeable love.<ref name="Saw Gerrera" /> After she was deposed and imprisoned by the Shadow Collective, Satine knew she had to contact Obi-Wan for help and did so during Korkie and Bo-Katan's failed rescue mission. Kenobi disobeyed orders to rescue her, and she was elated to see him.<ref name="The Lawless" /> They maintained their flirtatious banter even in the extreme circumstances and reminisced about their history together as they sped to escape Sundari.<ref name="Kenobi's Shadow" /> However, their escape was thwarted by Maul's forces, and they were brought to the palace, where he staged his long-sought revenge against Obi-Wan with Satine as his tool. Kryze used what little strength she had to tell Kenobi to stick to his beliefs, and with her dying words affirmed her love for him.<ref name="The Lawless" />

==Skills and abilities==
{{Quote|One can only survive the rigors of courtly formalities for so long.''"<br />"''We are of the same mind.|Both Senator Amidala and Duchess Satine often enjoyed the dangers they faced|<ref name="Corruption" />}}
[[File:BalutarClassSwoop-SWE.png|thumb|right|200px|Satine riding a Mandalorian speeder bike.]]
Despite her pacifist principles and abhorrence of violence, Kryze had some skill in combat and could hold her own in a fight. When freeing Obi-Wan from the mines on Concordia, Kryze was attacked by a pair of Death Watch soldiers, and she managed to hold them back on her own before Obi-Wan intervened.<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /> She was a sly combatant, displaying as much during her trip to Coruscant aboard the ''Coronet''. While fighting off the assassin droids, she and Obi-Wan weaved together back-to-back seamlessly, and she managed to grab Senator Merrik's blaster from him by stamping his foot then pulling herself out of his grasp in one swift move. Kryze was additionally capable of engaging in armed combat<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /> and had good aim with a blaster.<ref name="DoM" /> When questioned about her choice to carry a deactivator by Obi-Wan, Satine reasoned that even though she was a pacifist, she wasn't unwilling to defend herself.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /> Despite the dangers she often faced, the duchess enjoyed the adventure and risk she was involved in when it did not affect her people at large.<ref name="Corruption" />

As the ruler of Mandalore, Duchess Satine was strong-willed and determined, with proficiency in leadership, politics, and diplomacy.<ref name="Join the Battle" /> She was a gifted speaker and showed strength in analyzing her surroundings. She could even hold her own before the Galactic Senate when under pressure from Supreme Chancellor Palpatine and Vice Chair Amedda.<ref name="DoM" /> Due to the constant threats made to her life, she was a resilient woman and could withstand conditions as extreme as electric torture.<ref name="TA" /> Among her other abilities, Kryze could drive speeder bikes<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /> and could evidently fly spacecraft; during Obi-Wan's failed attempt to rescue her from imprisonment, she was prepared to co-pilot the ''Twilight'' but was forced to evacuate when the ship was damaged.<ref name="The Lawless" /> Satine was also multilingual. Though she primarily spoke using [[Galactic Basic Standard]], she was fluent in Concordian, a dialect of [[Mando'a]].<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|Do you always carry a deactivator?''"<br />"''Just because I'm a pacifist doesn't mean I won't defend myself!|Obi-Wan questions Satine's choice to carry a deactivator pistol|<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" />}}
As the ruler of Mandalore, Satine knew of the optics of her appearance and always took care to present herself with dignity and poise.<ref name="Kenobi's Shadow" /> Kryze fashioned her hair in a Kalevalan style and, in her wardrobe, made significant use of soothing<ref name="Join the Battle" /> and rich colors with floral-inspired designs meant to emulate the forests and lakes that once populated Mandalore's surface. Her elegant clothing,<ref name="Kenobi's Shadow" /> which rivaled that of even the infamously [[Padmé Amidala's wardrobe|elaborate wardrobe]] of Padmé Amidala,<ref name="Brotherhood" /> was not worn out of vanity but was strategically chosen to reflect Mandalore's past beauty and remind those who saw her of what the planet once was and what it could still be.<ref name="Kenobi's Shadow" /> Despite her staunch pacifist stance, Kryze always carried a deactivator hold-out pistol, a small but powerful blaster that fired energy shots that could deactivate droids.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" />

[[File:Mandalore_system.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Satine Kryze was the owner of the luxury yacht ''Coronet''.]]
Shortly after her ascent to the throne, Duchess Satine became the owner of<ref name="BMF 76">{{BuildFalconCite|76|Starship Fact File}}</ref> the [[Nau'ur-class yacht|''Nau'ur''-class yacht]]<ref name="S&S">''[[Starships and Speeders]]''</ref> ''Coronet'', a custom-built spaceliner manufactured by [[Kalevala Spaceworks]]. Built on Kryze's homeworld of Kalevala, the ''Coronet'' was designed with Satine's pacifist ideals in mind. The ship's distinctive design heavily reflected the hope that Mandalore would finally begin to prosper under her leadership. Elegant, versatile, and non-threatening in appearance, the ''Coronet'' expressed the qualities the new Mandalore looked to project to the galaxy with Satine as its leader. The craftsmanship of the ''Coronet'' was as utilitarian<ref name="BMF 76" /> as Kryze's clothing;<ref name="Kenobi's Shadow" /> the ship made heavy use of materials and traditional fabrics from all over the Mandalore sector and was meant to showcase all that the Mandalorian people had to offer the galaxy.<ref name="BMF 76" />

The upper section of the ''Coronet'' was home to Satine and her traveling retinue and included various amenities for the royal guests. The ''Coronet'' was staffed by numerous servant and protocol droids, including [[LEP-series service droid]]s<ref name="Join the Battle" /> and the more-advanced [[BD-3000 luxury droid]]. Though the ship's primary purpose was to be used as Kryze's personal transport for her and those that comprised her court, Satine ensured that the ''Coronet'' was not just a plaything of the elite but also a cheap mode of transportation for unwealthy travelers. The ''Coronet'' was a unique example of a vessel that combined functionality with an economic and political purpose. As a transport ship, Kryze's yacht allowed both Mandalorians and tourists passage throughout the Mandalore sector, which proved beneficial to the economies of several Mandalorian worlds, including Mandalore itself. Even after the fall of Kryze and the New Mandalorians, the ''Coronet'' continued to serve the Mandalorian people.<ref name="BMF 76" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Satine's a formidable woman in all regards—extremely intelligent, incorruptible, passionate and beautiful, with a great devotion to peace. She might come off as stuffy, but that is because she knows she's in a den of wolves and must appear powerful and unshakable. Throughout history, some of the most powerful figures—like Gandhi and Dr. King—were pacifists who literally changed the world by refusing to fight. There's so much fighting in ''The Clone Wars''; when someone is brave enough to speak up to try and stop it, that voice becomes like a light in the darkness, strong and memorable.|Henry Gilroy on the character of Satine Kryze|<ref name="Obi-Wan Kenobi's Past">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news/news20100201/index.html|text=Obi-Wan Kenobi's Past Resurfaces in ''The Clone Wars''}}</ref>}}
Satine Kryze first appeared in "[[The Mandalore Plot]]," the twelfth episode of the [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]] of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''. The episode was directed by [[Kyle Dunlevy]], written by [[Melinda Hsu]] and [[Drew Z. Greenberg]],<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /> and first aired on [[January 29]], [[2010]].<ref name="MandalorePlotArc">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode212.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: The Mandalore Plot}}</ref> "The Mandalore Plot" was the first in a trilogy of episodes, followed by "[[Voyage of Temptation]]" and "[[Duchess of Mandalore]]." Initially, "Voyage of Temptation" was the only episode planned to feature either Satine or the Mandalorian storyline,<ref name="Insider 117">{{InsiderCite|117|The Duchess and the Jedi}}</ref> but at the insistence of writer [[Henry Gilroy]] and supervising director [[Dave Filoni]], who wanted to feature more of the Mandalorians in ''The Clone Wars'',<ref name="Insider 115">{{InsiderCite|115|Ready for Battle!}}</ref> series creator [[George Lucas]] decided to develop on the story of "Voyage of Temptation" and create a three-part episodic arc from it,<ref name="Insider 117" /> in part because he was interested in exploring more of the social and political aspects of Duchess Satine's character.<ref name="Conversations">{{YouTube|video=Lyluvbs-ByM|text=Clone Wars Conversations Episode 1: "The Duchess & The Jedi"|channel=@JamesArnoldTaylor|name=James Arnold Taylor}}</ref> As a result, "The Mandalore Plot" and "Duchess of Mandalore" entered production.<ref name="Insider 117" />

The idea to give Obi-Wan Kenobi a romantic interest in ''The Clone Wars'' came from Henry Gilroy, who also worked as a story editor.<ref name="The Lawless Episode Guide">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/the-lawless-episode-guide|text="The Lawless" Episode Guide | The Clone Wars}}</ref> Satine's design was based off of unused concept art of [[Queen]] Padmé Amidala for [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] illustrated by [[Iain McCaig]].<ref name="The Mandalore Plot Trivia Gallery">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/the-mandalore-plot-trivia-gallery|text="The Mandalore Plot" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|slide 4}}</ref> She was inspired by [[Wikipedia:Cate Blanchett|Cate Blanchett]], particularly her performance as [[Wikipedia:Elizabeth I|Queen Elizabeth I]], whom she portrayed in [[Wikipedia:Elizabeth (film)|''Elizabeth'']] and [[Wikipedia:Elizabeth: The Golden Age|''Elizabeth: The Golden Age'']].<ref name="IGN Interview">{{WebCite|url=http://uk.ign.com/articles/2010/01/28/star-wars-are-you-ready-for-the-mandalorians?page=2|text=Star Wars: Are You Ready for the Mandalorians?|date=2010-01-28|archivedate=20200519092547}}</ref> Gilroy further compared Satine's character to real-life pacifists [[Wikipedia:Mahatma Gandhi|Mahatma Gandhi]] and [[Wikipedia:Martin Luther King Jr.|Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.]], believing that Satine's powerful devotion made her stand out amongst the violence depicted in ''The Clone Wars''.<ref name="Obi-Wan Kenobi's Past" /> Gilroy, who created her name, denied that Satine was named after [[Wikipedia:Nicole Kidman|Nicole Kidman's]] character in [[Wikipedia:Moulin Rouge!|''Moulin Rouge!'']], who was the love interest of [[Ewan McGregor]]'s character. In response, Dave Filoni said he did not realize this at first, and stated, "I still wanna question Gilroy about that, because I'm like, 'Come on, really? I mean, out of all the names, really?' It's pretty weird, I'll give you that."<ref name="IGN Interview" />

[[File:Graves.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Duchess Satine was voiced by Anna Graves in ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''.]]
Duchess Satine is portrayed in ''The Clone Wars'' by voice actress [[Anna Graves]]. Having grown up a ''[[Star Wars]]'' fan, Graves was interested in voicing a role in the yet-unreleased ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''. She auditioned for the role of Satine, at that point set to only feature in "Voyage of Temptation," and sent her audition tape to [[Lucasfilm]] in [[2007]] and earned a callback at L.A. Studios from casting director [[Susan Blu]]. According to Graves, the team behind ''The Clone Wars'' wanted an actor who could portray Satine with a "regal, royal, down-to-earth" voice similar to Blanchett's.<ref name="Conversations" /> Following Filoni's direction, Graves tried to deliver some of Satine's speeches with the same gravitas as Blanchett's performance as Elizabeth I. She also used the bickering relationship between Princess Leia Organa and [[Han Solo]] in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] as a basis for her voice work, wanting the character of Satine to challenge Obi-Wan as much as Organa challenged Solo.<ref name="Insider 117" /> Voiceover sessions for ''The Clone Wars'' were recorded by the production team, and, according to Graves, this lent to the animated Satine sharing some of her expressions and mannerisms.<ref name="Conversations" />

At the time of her audition, Graves was unaware that the character would be a love interest for Obi-Wan Kenobi, but even after learning this was still drawn to the character<ref name="Conversations" /> because, despite her deep connection to the story of Obi-Wan, Satine stood out to Graves as someone who was not reliant on the narrative of another character to shine. Although initially unaware of the history and culture of the Mandalorians, Graves educated herself upon landing the role. By the time of recording, Graves understood the importance of her role and was "excited to speak in the Concordian dialect."<ref name="Insider 117" /> From the conception of the character, the creatives behind ''The Clone Wars'' intended for Satine to be killed off.<ref name="The Lawless Episode Guide" /> Although the voice performers for ''The Clone Wars'' were usually given scripts on the day of recording, Graves was informed of Satine's fate by Filoni long before recording for the [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|season five]] episode "[[The Lawless]]" began, as far back as subtle hints from Filoni during the production of [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|season three]].<ref name="Conversations" />

Early plans of the ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' episode "[[Twin Suns (episode)|Twin Suns]]" featured Maul experiencing [[Force vision|visions]] of both Kryze and Savage Opress before facing Obi-Wan Kenobi on Tatooine. Unlike Opress, who made it as far as the design phase, Satine was cut from production early on.<ref name="SWCO 2017">{{SW|url=news/swco-2017-11-things-we-learned-from-dave-filoni-and-pablo-hidalgos-animated-origins-and-unexpected-fates-panel|text=SWCO 2017: 11 Things We Learned from Dave Filoni and Pablo Hidalgo's "Animated Origins and Unexpected Fates" Panel}}</ref>

In her entry in the [[Encyclopedia (StarWars.com)|Encyclopedia]], Satine's [[homeworld]] was listed as being Mandalore.<ref name="SWE" /> However, Tal Merrik's [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] entry correctly lists her homeworld as Kalevala.<ref name="TalMerrikDB" />
